**1.5h**

For today, I mostly just decided to stick with doing a bit of research. The first couple of things that I looked through were some rather simple additions to the project, like backlit switches and the like.
(Like this!) ->

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/ec064ec4fc10eb5d38f0ca3daf2b14109c1879a988fdb4a4a5d269e5b2ca23dc.png)

But then I thought about maybe adding in a small lcd screen to act as a visualizer, or at the very least display some data. I decided to stick with the data side of things, mostly because implementing a visualizer would force me to add on some more components, which might strain my budget.

### 2026-10-24 – So today, I wanted to focus on finishing the basic project for the PCB.

**4h**

So today, I wanted to focus on finishing the basic project for the PCB.

I started off by making the pads for the keypad themselves. I took some liberties with the design though.

![FingerPad](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/b4eebaee4fc9c8422341f5057991d8f64346f5f6d71aa9f9b275a112f0484cda.png)

The main reason why I designed it the way I did was because I wanted to have it be relatively unique, and still be intuitive to use.

![IntialPCBconfig](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/0f84106c2a89c2bbe7b8886f66f6343e338f6ec0ec362d61f3503508146fb576.png)

The four pads in the middle are for all of your fingers to hover over (excluding your thumb, that rests over the pad to the side.) Then, whenever you want to touch the two panels on the top or bottom, you can just shift your fingers up and down! One issue is the fact that the orientation is mostly for right-handed people, so I might go back and make a different orientation for lefties.

After that, I added it to the rest of my PCB, and made sure to orient it in a way that would make routing easier in the future.

And with that, I had to finally start routing. (Yay.....)

It gave me a bit of trouble like usual, and I had to go back to the schematics to make sure everything worked properly, but I did manage to get everything to work out in the end.

![IntialPCBRouting](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/ed2bb178b386e5c44c6e15ead53839eb98a1b8d7f8f4adc656eeaf7f6f536647.png)

Here's what the PCB looks like currently:

![3d_PCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/387befff85454ec31eeab8d6ff2864f86572a1c64445fc693b9d487119426ba3.png)

After that, I started on my research for the display.

To make sure that I'd know when i found my boundaries, I thought up a couple questions that I knew I needed to answer before I started on the display:

Does the Microcontroller support it?

How would I go about doing it in the first place?

What's going to be on the display? (Notes, or something else?)

What would be the cheapest implementation?

How much would I need to edit the PCB?

and so on.

After I compiled these questions, I took care of the 5-hour checkpoint, and then I decided it was about time to head to bed.

### 2026-10-25 – I started on the research first today, and what I found was certainly interesting. The XIAO ESP32-S3 has some versions that come with a microphone, but the version that I'm planning on making does not

**3.5h**

I started on the research first today, and what I found was certainly interesting. The XIAO ESP32-S3 has some versions that come with a microphone, but the version that I'm planning on making does not. I also couldn't really find anything that would allow me to add a display easily.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/e5eb6b60b33b95fe5ffb23b52d7def74ff9d9f9e8cb0c30ff7301d0ad9a6c2e6.png)
(I was considering getting the sense, but  I'm already kinda pushing it on the budget..)

 So, now, what I'm planning on doing is using some LEDS that will correspond with each pad being pressed, so the user will be able to tell which note they're playing a little easier.

LEDS shouldn't necessarily be too expensive, and  I can also probably easily figure out how to get everything to work relatively easily.

But first, I thought it'd be nice to make some art for the board, so I did.
These are the two icons that I ended up making:

![MidiKeyIcon2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/e042b189a9dec7aa9e5993474b58f3e0833114abf93e26a1e06b16dcc84c5576.png)

![MidiKeyIcon1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/b2527eec6dac4dd698ed0e2ec5ff9f131bc31cc26e32cb2aeb426b2c8f6b33a0.png)

I then added them to the PCB board, and after that, I got started on the LEDs.

I had a bit of trouble figuring out exactly which ones would be a good fit, but I eventually decided on one, and added it to the board.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/5ea99c451706aeecbdd66c6860f64c5c2f16d8746b15a28c5ab147368cde50d2.png)

After that, it was well past midnight, so I decided to leave the routing, and the exporting for tomorrow morning.
